about: Five merged (or closed) PRs whose ground truth is Hare's own ledger, docs/hare-ledger.json, not a third-party bot. Each case lists what Hare posted on that PR and what became of it, so a rerun can be scored against a known truth rather than against another model's opinion. Chosen because between them they carry the three outcomes a proof has to separate: a real finding that was right and got fixed or resolved (#245, #247, #248), a real finding the owner judged wrong (#258), and a real finding on a PR that closed unmerged (#237). Every case is scored the same way scripts/hare_eval.py scores docs/hare-eval-cases.json: a finding catches an expected issue when it names the same file (and a line within 25, when one is given) and its text carries one of the words.
truth_from: docs/hare-ledger.json (built by scripts/hare_ledger.py from the notes, the Since lines and resolved threads)

cases.head: 944ef4d
cases.note: One real finding, judged right, thread resolved. The ledger's `resolved` fate means the finding's thread was resolved on GitHub.

expect.what: `stitched` is never assigned when the restart is not longer than the kept findings, so the later read raises UnboundLocalError

cases.head: 2d26fa8
cases.note: One real finding, judged right, thread resolved.

expect.what: the provider chain order changes without a PLAN entry, which the repo's scope rules call out

cases.head: 031b6ff
cases.note: One real finding, judged right, fixed by the author. The second row is a skip the ledger kept open; it is listed so a rerun that reproduces it is not counted as a false alarm.

expect.what: `apply_rules` anchors on a header string that does not match the real header, so the block lands at the end of the file
the title says AGENTS.md and the change moves the rules to HARE.md

cases.head: 99fb7ef
cases.note: The one case with a known WRONG finding. The ledger records `wrong`, so any run that reproduces it as `real` is making the same mistake again, and any run that does not reproduce it has removed a false alarm. This is the row that separates a better review from a different review.

expect.what: the test asserts three calls but the chain order fires four hops before g1 answers
the added failover line is over 80 characters
the new comment is over 80 characters

cases.head: bbce985
cases.note: Closed unmerged, so every finding's fate is `dropped`. The real one is still the known truth for what was wrong in that diff; the drops are about what happened to the PR, not about whether the finding was right.

expect.what: the fence regex matches a literal backslash, so the fence path is dead code and the test passes only because json_objects covers the case
the test inspects co_varnames instead of calling the function, so it passes even if the parameter is ignored
